Furthermore, we showcase case studies and MetaKG applications in e-commerce, smart cities, healthcare, and entertainment. We provide a starting point for creating reliable and efficient MetaKGs that serve a range of applications and domains.

articleTitle: A Deep Transfer Learning Model for Classifying Alzheimer's Disease Using MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) affects the cells of the human brain and leads to the development of dementia. The progressive brain cells degeneration results in the inability to carry out everyday duties. The therapy for this condition is currently insufficiently developed. Nevertheless, detecting the AD at an early stage can help control its transmission. To detect AD at an early stage using brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), it is necessary to create an automated system that can identify and categorize individuals with dementia. In this research, a deep learning (DL) model is developed for the classification of AD based on MRI pictures. The research model was created by applying a pre-trained transfer learning model known as ResNeXt-101. The OASIS-3 dataset of MRI images is initially gathered and utilized for both training the model and evaluating its performance. The dataset comprises 2842 MRI pictures pertaining to AD and its different phases. As part of the preprocessing stage, all the images are resized and cropped to a uniform size of 224×224 pixels. Furthermore, they are enhanced utilizing the contrast enhancement technique. The ResU-Net segmentation method is utilized following the preprocessing phase. The ResNeXt-101 model is employed for the purpose of classification the segmented images. The MRI pictures are divided into training and testing sets, with 75% allotted to train the model and 25% allocated to evaluate the model. The classification is conducted using a binary approach, categorizing the data as either the presence or absence of AD. The research model's performance was evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, f1-score, and precision. The research model achieved a training accuracy of 99.67%, sensitivity of 99.54%, precision of 99.72%, specificity of 99.41%, and a f1-score of 99.60%. The model achieved an accuracy of 99.38%, a sensitivity of 98.29%, a precision of 99.40%, a specificity of 99.24%, and a f1-score of 99.36% in the performance evaluation. The test results were compared to the existing models for validation. The research model has demonstrated superior performance when compared to all the other models.

articleTitle: Transforming Tourism: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Innovation in Saudi Arabia
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in the tourism industry has emerged as a focal point of research and discourse, promising transformative impacts across various facets of the sector. This study delves into the multifaceted dimensions surrounding AI integration in the context of the tourism industry, with a specific focus on Saudi Arabia. Central to the investigation are key themes encompassing perceptions, challenges, opportunities, ethical implications, organizational adaptation, and future directions. Through a combination of conceptual analysis and empirical inquiry, this research aims to unravel stakeholders' attitudes, beliefs, and expectations regarding AI's role and impact in tourism while also elucidating the technical, organizational, and cultural barriers hindering effective AI adoption. Moreover, the study explores the vast opportunities AI presents for enhancing operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, and competitive advantage within the Saudi Arabian tourism landscape. Ethical considerations pertaining to data privacy, algorithmic bias, and societal impacts are critically examined, alongside insights into organizational adaptation strategies required to leverage AI technologies effectively. Furthermore, the research endeavors to provide foresight into future directions of AI-driven tourism innovation, shedding light on emerging trends, regulatory frameworks, and technological advancements shaping the trajectory of the industry. By synthesizing conceptual analysis with empirical findings, this study aims to offer valuable insights and strategic guidance for stakeholders navigating the evolving AI landscape in the tourism sector of Saudi Arabia.

articleTitle: UrbanPark: Advancing Parking Infrastructure with LoRaWAN-Enabled Smart Parking Modules
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to address the escalating challenges in urban parking management by developing a LoRaWAN-based autonomous smart parking system (UrbanPark). With urbanization and increased vehicle populations, there is a pressing need for innovative solutions to optimize resource utilization and enhance user experience of vehicle parking. Leveraging the capabilities of Long-Range Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN), this system integrates a mobile application, a web-based interface, and LoRaWAN-enabled smart parking modules to provide users and administrators with real-time parking space availability information. The mobile application offers a user-friendly interface for drivers to locate and reserve parking spaces, while the web-based interface empowers administrators with comprehensive oversight and management functionalities. The LoRaWAN-enabled smart parking modules autonomously monitor parking space occupancy and transmit data efficiently over long distances with minimal energy consumption and are implemented in Raspberry Pi as the server. Through this integration, the system offers scalable, cost-effective, and sustainable solutions to urban parking management challenges, contributing to the development of smarter, more connected urban environments.

articleTitle: DL-MD: Leveraging LSTM and GRU for Cutting-Edge Malware Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In the field of cyber-security, identifying and combating malware threats continues to pose a significant challenge. While traditional techniques like signature detection and behavioral analysis have shown success, they struggle to keep up with the evolving landscape of malware variations. Additionally, although traditional clustering algorithms have been beneficial, the increasing volume and complexity of malware threats have rendered these techniques less accurate and effective in malware detection. This paper introduces an innovative approach for detecting harmful software within executable files. Our approach diverges significantly from traditional malware detection systems, which typically rely on signatures. Instead, we employ Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) algorithms to differentiate between malicious and benign files. Our experiments demonstrate that our Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models, followed by traditional clustering algorithms, significantly and effectively aid in discerning between malicious and benign files. This approach benefits from the combination of advanced deep learning techniques and traditional clustering methods. Our experiments show that the GRU model slightly outperformed the LSTM model in terms of accuracy while both GRU and LSTM models perform much better than using only traditional clustering algorithms. The effectiveness of our approach was tested across three different datasets. This work also highlights the potential of deep learning techniques, especially RNN algorithms, in strengthening information security and cyber-security defenses in today's era.

articleTitle: Classification of Alzheimer's Disease using Attention UNet-MobileNet Model
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (ALD) is a degenerative and incurable neurological condition that impacts many individuals globally. Early identification and precise diagnosis of ALD are essential for efficient therapy and control of the condition. This research presents a transfer learning-based method for diagnosing ALD using magnetic resonance image (MRI) data. This research introduced a deep learning (DL) model known as MobileNet-v2 to accurately classify ALD using MRI images. The classification task involves the use of MIRIAD, a dataset consisting of MRI images specifically related to ALD. The collection comprises 708 MRI pictures pertaining to ALD and its different phases. The MRI pictures undergo preprocessing and are then split into training and testing sets, with 70% allocated for training and 30% for testing. Following the preprocessing stage, the segmentation procedure is carried out with the Attention UNet architecture. The segmented images are inputted into the MobileNet-v2 model for ALD classification. The classification is conducted as a binary classification, categorizing the data as either the presence or absence of ALD. The research model's performances are evaluated based on metrics including accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, f1-scores, and precision. The test results were compared to the existing models for validation. The research model has demonstrated superior performance when compared to all other models.

articleTitle: NAMAQ - Arabic Handwriting Recognition Using Deep Learning, AI, and ML with Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The Arabic language is one of the delicate languages in terms of usage. Many characters in the language make it difficult for management to identify the script quickly. The holy book of the Muslims, the Quran, is written in Arabic. Several valuable resources from ancient and present times have helpful information on Arabic. The handwritten scripts vary from person to person, and it is not simple to understand and realize what is mentioned inside the scripts. In this study, the main emphasis is on recognizing Arabic handwritten words. The convolution neural network (CNN) is used, and feature extraction is done with the help of CNN for the Arabic text images uploaded into the system. With the help of machine learning classifiers, these handwritten scripts are recognized for similarity from the training data set. A recognition rate of up to 96.4% for 29 classes is achieved. The proposed model is tested using large datasets of characters and formations in the Arabic language. The identified features are further passed on to the machine learning classification model. Various researchers have worked on several models that yield variable rates of recognition. The highest rate is received at 96.3%. The next phase of the model proposed in this study focuses on the sentiment analysis of the scripts or texts classified in the recognition phase. The author's sentiment is identified for classifying the results.

articleTitle: The Influence of Computer-Assisted Language Learning (CALL) on Writing Skills and Attitudes of First-Year EFL Students at the University of Tabuk
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In the current educational environment, Computer-Assisted Language Learning (CALL) has become a significant method for enhancing students' English language acquisition and engagement. This research at the University of Tabuk aimed to evaluate the effect of CALL on the English proficiency and attitudes of first-year students. The study utilized a pre-test and post-test design along with a survey questionnaire, with participants randomly assigned to either the experimental or control group from a population of 240 first-year students across six classes during the 2021–2022 academic year. The results demonstrated that CALL positively influenced the English language performance and attitudes of first-year students. Statistical analysis using SPSS 22.0 showed a p-value of 0.00, which is below the significance threshold of 0.05, supporting the acceptance of the alternative hypothesis (H1) and the rejection of the null hypothesis (HO). Additionally, students displayed a positive attitude towards learning English with CALL, with no negative feedback reported. The study also discussed the implications and limitations of these findings.

articleTitle: UNet-CrossViT: A Deep Learning Model for Classifying Alzheimer's Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In recent times, deep-learning (DL) methods are implemented to classify neuroimaging data associated with Alzheimer's disease (AZD), and notable advancements have been achieved. Traditional Machine Learning (ML) has been shown to be helpful in aiding the diagnosis of AZD, however only a limited number of research have explored the capabilities of DL and deep transfer learning (DTL) in this intricate process. In this research, a novel DTL model called Cross attention multi scale Vision Transformer (CrossViT) is proposed to classify the AZD using MRI images. For this classification, a set of MRI images of AZD is collected from the Kaggle website. The collected dataset has 6400 images of MRI related to AZD and its various stages. The MRI images are preprocessed and divided into training and testing sets as 80% and 20%. After preprocessing, the segmentation is performed using the UNet architecture. The segmented images are fed to the proposed CrossViT model for AZD classification. The classification is performed as a binary classification, as it classified the results as either the AZD is present or not. The performances of the research model are assessed based on accuracy, specificity, sensitivity, f1-score, and precision. The research model has attained 99.63% accuracy, 99.51% sensitivity, 99.69% precision, 99.35% specificity, and 99.50% f1-score in training. The model attained 99.21% accuracy, 98.94% sensitivity, 99.25% precision, 99.10% specificity, and 99.04% f1-score in testing. The test results were compared with the current models for validation. The research model has outperformed all the compared model in comparison.

articleTitle: Power Factor Improvement in Regional Distribution Feeders with Optimal Allocation of Distributed Generators and Shunt Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper critically assesses power factor (pf) compensation techniques for the regional distribution feeders, focusing on Distributed Generators (DGs) and shunt capacitors. Therefore, the research aims to identify the potential of distribution networks to maximize efficiency by combining the Backward Forward Sweep (BFS) with the Sea Horse Optimization (SHO) algorithm. Through extensive testing using Torrit software and the MATPOWER toolbox, the study primarily focuses on two scenarios: one type of the DGs known as type 2 DGs, which only injects the reactive power. One of the scenarios includes Q as a shunt capacitance, while the second model represents type 3 DGs that supply both active power (P) and reactive power (Q). The type 2 DG deployment reduces the reactive power loss in the network. On the other hand, the use of type 3 DGs leads to a significant enhancement of pf as well as enhancement of the voltage profile. Most notably, coordinating type 3 DGs with shunt capacitors reveals that they work well hand in hand, contributing to better network improvement. This study offers a specific analysis of DGs deployment for utility operators and presents a roadmap for aiding their decision-making process in efficiently analyzing power systems' optimization.

articleTitle: AI-Empowered ClimateClean: Wastewater-to-Energy Solutions for a Resilient and Sustainable Future
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Wastewater treatment has emerged as a critical area of interest for sustainable resource management due to its ability to provide both environmental repair and produce renewable energy. Using artificial intelligence (AI) to boost efficacy and efficiency, this study explores wastewater-to-energy solutions from the standpoint of sustainable development and climate change mitigation. We analyse the energy outputs, advantages, and climatic implications, including Microbial Fuel Cells (MFC), Thermal Conversion (TC), Anaerobic Digestion (AD), and Hydrothermal Processes (HP) while providing a taxonomy and integrating AI-driven strategies for optimisation. By utilizing state-of-the-art research and practical implementations, we clarify optimal procedures, valuable insights, and critical success elements influencing the implementation. To manage resources sustainably, this paper emphasizes incorporating wastewater-to-energy solutions into current infrastructure wastewater-to-energy paradigms, encouraging multi-stakeholder involvement, and igniting circular economy ideas. It provides strategic guidance for negotiating complex technical and legal environments, pointing the way toward the scalable and significant implementation of wastewater-to-energy breakthroughs to achieve a more sustainable, resilient, and clean future in the face of climate change.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of AES, RC and Twofish Algorithms for Data Encryption and Decryption
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of three widely used encryption algorithms, namely AES (Advanced Encryption Standard), RC (Rivest Cipher), and Twofish, with a focus on their performance in data encryption and decryption. The study aims to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of these algorithms in terms of security, speed, and efficiency. The analysis involves benchmarking the algorithms against various performance metrics, including encryption time, decryption time, key size, and resistance against cryptanalysis attacks. Additionally, the research explores the impact of different data sizes and configurations on the performance of each algorithm. The findings of this study will provide valuable insights for decision-makers and practitioners in selecting the most suitable encryption algorithm for their specific needs, considering the tradeoffs between security and performance.

articleTitle: An Improved Machine Learning-Driven Glaucoma Diagnostic Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Glaucoma is a progressive eye condition that impairs the optic nerve and is often called a “silent thief of sight.” The increasing number of individuals losing their vision due to this condition is a cause for concern. Research is being conducted to develop computer-aided systems that can help ophthalmologists in the early diagnosis of glaucoma. OD and OC are often compared to calculate the cup-to-disc (CDR) ratio, indicating whether the eye is glaucomatous. This study presents a novel methodology for segmenting the optic disc (OD) and optic cup (OC). We propose a modified version of the ResUNet architecture. ResUNet is a convolutional neural network architecture that combines residual learning and U-Net architecture for semantic segmentation tasks, offering improved performance in capturing fine details and spatial context. Our proposed model's performance was evaluated on the DRISHTIGS publicly available dataset, and an IOU score of 94.5% and 89.1% were achieved for OD and OC segmentation, respectively.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology? Visual Art Marketing Through Non-Fungible Token (NFT) from the Perspectives of Islamic Shariah in Malaysia: A Need Assessment Analyses
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The development of blockchain technology across the globe has seen to be vast, including those related to visual arts. In Islam, anything new: especially those that never existed before, needs to be, obligatory discussed from the Islamic Shariah perspective. Therefore, the vast development of blockchain technology relating to non-fungible token (NFT) towards marketing visual art needs assessment from the Islamic Shariah perspective as there has not been any empirical studies carried out towards it. This paper intends to discuss a need assessment analyses regarding marketing visual art through the NFT platform blockchain technology from the Islamic Shariah perspective in Malaysia. Using the systematic literature review technique, researchers have discussed briefly regarding the development of visual arts, NFT and its trend, and reviewing Islamic perspectives on NFT. As a result, it is necessary for the Islamic Council of Malaysia to explain in detail the marketing of visual arts through NFT. A proper paperwork is crucial to give an overview on the practices regarding NFT that are 1) crypto currency; 2) artwork visual appearance; 3) copyright and consent issue; 4) pricing and value; and 5) royalty and blockchain record - to market of visual arts for Islamic Shariah assessment; in ensuring the muamalat activities amongst Muslims are centred on the faith of Islam.

articleTitle: IoT Device Classification Using Hybrid Stacking Machine Learning Model on IoT Network Traffic Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In the expanding domain of the Internet of Things (IoT), accurately classifying devices is essential for ensuring secure and efficient network management. As IoT networks increase in size and complexity, the challenge of effectively managing these devices becomes more pressing, particularly in defending against the risks posed by Shadow IoT devices unauthorized devices that connect to networks without formal approval. Despite some progress, previous research has largely focused on individual machine learning algorithms or simple ensemble models, with limited exploration of hybrid stacking models that combine two classifiers. This leaves a gap in understanding how different classifier combinations can balance accuracy, training time, and prediction time. This thesis addresses these gaps by using a hybrid stacking machine learning model that integrates two classifiers with the focus on reducing training and prediction times while maintaining or improving classification accuracy. The results show significant improvements in existing models. Combination of Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost (RFXGB) achieved a test accuracy of 72.4% and a training accuracy of 99.2%, with a training time of 4.17 seconds and a prediction time of 0.053 seconds, marking a 7.4% increase in test accuracy compared to the single XGBoost classifier. Similarly, the combination of Random Forest and Support Vector Machine (RFSVM) achieved a test accuracy of 71.2% and a training accuracy of 99.6%, with a training time of 2.196 seconds and a prediction time of 0.051 seconds, showing a 12.6% improvement in test accuracy over the single Support Vector Machine classifier.

articleTitle: Text-Bullying Detection in Online Social Networks Using Two Levels Ensemble Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Increasing use of online social networks and their popularity have provided us with immeasurable options, and the benefits are undeniable. However, people may be embarrassed, insulted, bullied, and harassed by anonymous users, strangers, or peers, degrading these benefits. As a result, there is a significant need to identify, control, and restrict the transmission of bullying information on social networking sites, thus motivating us to perform this study to automate cyberbullying detection. In this paper, we develop a Two Levels Ensemble Detection Bullying (TLEDB) model to detect online text bullying and abusive messages. For this, we select three Machine Learning classifiers and three ensemble models with two feature extraction techniques, namely TF-IDF and Bag of Words (BoW). Experimental results show that our proposed TLEDB model generates the best performance of 98.73% when applying the TF-IDF feature with K-Fold cross-validation and gives an accuracy of 97.55 % when using the BoW feature with Stratified K-fold cross-validation.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna SAR-Based Imaging System for Structural Health Monitoring Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR) based microwave imaging systems for non-destructive testing and evaluation (NDT&E) applications, the antenna plays a crucial role in determining the system's ability to detect defects in materials for structural health monitoring. Traditional antennas for SAR-based NDT&E often rely on narrow beam antennas such as an open-ended waveguide (OEW), which is costly and impractical for far-field inspections utilizing reflection mode. This paper proposes the design and implementation of a robust and cost-effective antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) that outperforms OEW in far-field NDT&E inspections. The performance of the AVA is evaluated against OEW through simulation and experimental studies. Defective sample images were reconstructed using the autofocus range-Doppler algorithm (RDA). The results obtained demonstrated that both the OEW and AVA successfully reconstructed the defective images under test. However, at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) and far-field inspection, the OEW performance degraded significantly. In contrast, the AVA with its exponentially tapered slot antenna design, provided a more directive and broadband radiation pattern, featuring low side lobe levels and consistent beamwidth over a wide frequency range. Consequently, the AVA achieved a superior SNR of 2 dB, compared to OEW's -5 dB. These findings suggest that the AVA design is a more effective solution for SAR-based structural health monitoring in far-field NDT&E applications.

articleTitle: Detecting Depression in Arabic Texts Using AI Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In Arabic-speaking communities, mental health issues often go unrecognized due to cultural stigma and a lack of awareness, making early diagnosis challenging. Social media platforms and online forums provide a rich source of data that can be used to identify early signs of depression through analysis of user-generated content. This study aimed to develop a reliable method for detecting depressive tendencies in Arabic texts using artificial intelligence techniques. To achieve this, we collected approximately 19,000 posts from the Arabic forum “Nafsany,” using Python's BeautifulSoup library to scrape data based on keywords related to depression. The data were annotated with the help of an expert psychologist and classified according to the DSM-5 guidelines. Our study employed lexicon-based, machine learning, and deep learning approaches. An ensemble model combining various deep learning techniques was developed to enhance the accuracy of depression detection. The ensemble model achieved superior performance, with an accuracy of 93.03% and an F1-score of 92.93%, which demonstrates its effectiveness. This research is significant as it contributes to the early detection of depression in Arabic-speaking populations, potentially reducing stigma and barriers to mental health care. By improving the diagnostic methods, this study supports better mental health outcomes and provides a foundation for future research in the field.

articleTitle: Vision-Based Robust Lane Detection and Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Lane detection and tracking are crucial for modern vehicle navigation systems, especially for ADAS and autonomous vehicles. Traditional methods often fail under adverse conditions such as poor lighting, bad weather, and inconsistent road markings. This paper presents a novel approach using YOLOv5, an advanced object detection model known for its real-time performance and accuracy, to detect lane boundaries directly from images. We improved its robustness in challenging scenarios by adapting YOLOv5 for lane detection and introducing innovative post-processing techniques. These techniques include refining lane predictions, handling occlusions, and reducing noise. Extensive experiments on datasets from various conditions (daytime, nighttime, and adverse weather) show that our method outperforms existing approaches. The proposed YOLOv5-based system offers a promising solution for real-world driving challenges, enhancing the precision and dependability of lane recognition and tracking and positively impacting road safety and autonomous vehicle technologies.

articleTitle: 360 Roaming: A Software Engineering Approach Using Virtual Exploration and Real-world Travel
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's tourism industry has changed significantly in recent years. Launched in 2016, the Saudi Vision 2030 has played a significant role in achieving significant development and improving the tourism sector. Tourism is one of the main pillars of this vision. One of the main objectives of tourism development in Saudi Arabia is to attract international tourism and promote domestic tourism. In this research, a platform for domestic tourism in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia enhanced with virtual reality technology was designed. The study covers several topics that help travelers narrow down their vacation options by making travel and hotel reservations easier, giving them access to a virtual tour of the kingdom's most popular tourist destinations, and more. Additionally, the platform provides hotel and airline registration, promotional offers, and exclusive discounts. Furthermore, it ensures the reliability and reputation of hotels and airlines, aiming to prevent tourists from falling victim to scams and fraud through fake websites. In addition, it safeguards the standing and dependability of lodging facilities and airlines, hoping to keep travelers from becoming victims of fraud and swindles via phony websites.

articleTitle: Sales Forecasting in Retail Using Random Forest Regression: A Case Study on Walmart
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Accurate sales forecasting is crucial for retail giants like Walmart to optimize inventory management, plan operations, and enhance customer satisfaction. This study aims to develop a robust machine learning model for predicting weekly sales at Walmart stores, focusing on identifying the most important predictive features and utilizing the Random Forest Regressor. Using a comprehensive dataset from Kaggle, we conducted thorough data preprocessing, including addressing missing values and encoding categorical variables. Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE) was employed to determine the most significant features. The Random Forest Regressor, chosen for its ability to handle complex relationships, was parameterized with 100 estimators and evaluated using metrics such as Mean Squared Error (MSE), Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and R-squared (R2) score. The model achieved an R2 score of 0.9741, significantly outperforming a baseline model. Diagnostic plots confirmed the model's robustness, with errors following a normal distribution and residuals showing no discernible patterns. This research demonstrates the efficacy of machine learning, particularly the Random Forest Regressor, in enhancing sales forecasting accuracy in the retail sector, providing insights into feature importance and supporting strategic decision-making for inventory and operational planning. The paper concludes that the Random Forest Regressor significantly enhances Walmart's sales forecasting accuracy with a high R-squared score of 0.9741, outperforming baseline models and demonstrating robust predictive performance.

articleTitle: Exploring Coexistence of Digital Terrestrial Television and IMT Within 470-690 MHz Band: A Comprehensive Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In recent years, the increasing demand for mobile services has necessitated the exploration of new frequency bands to support the growth of the international mobile telecommunications (IMT) system. This article investigates the coexistence of digital terrestrial television (DTT) and IMT within the 470–690 MHz band, commonly referred to digital dividend (DD) bands. The study provides a comprehensive state-of-the-art analysis of existing literature on this topic, focuses on addressing the challenges, explores mitigation strategies to facilitate the harmonious coexistence of diverse services, and highlights potential avenues for future research. The outcomes of this paper aim to contribute to the ongoing international efforts that allow coexistence between different services and promote sustainable network advancement.

articleTitle: A Fuzzy-Based System for Water pH and Conductivity Level Management
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Maintaining pH, conductivity, and water tank levels is essential for water quality in industrial heat transfer applications. Traditional Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers may struggle to manage nonlinear relationships and process dynamics. To address this challenge, this paper proposes using a Mamdani-type Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) designed specifically for industrial settings. The FLC uses sensor data to regulate control valves and achieve the desired water quality and quantity. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the FLC in managing complex industrial water systems.

articleTitle: Developed a Multiple Ratchet Group Key Agreement Protocol
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Secure and scalable group key agreements provide end-to-end encryption in instant messaging applications and adapt to the frequently dynamic changes during chat life while maintaining the security features provided by the double ratchet protocol in one-on-one communication, represents a challenge. Using the Double Ratchet Algorithm approach and the core principles of confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity based on Chacha20/Poly1305, SHA256, and XEdDSA, respectively in addition to Curve2559 as an asymmetric system, this study introduces a secure, scalable, and flexible multiple ratchet group key agreement (MRGKA) protocol. MRGKA innovatively divides users into subgroups (SG), each with a maximum capacity of 15 members, and each subgroup is endowed with a unique Identity Key (SGIK) and Signed Pre-shared Keys (SGSPK), facilitating secure and private intra-group communications as if each subgroup were a single user entity. MRGKA provides an efficient 70 subgroup with a 20MB data size without any compression or cache mechanisms. Invite Authentication Code (IAC) was introduced in this protocol to provide robust subsequent sessions and more security strength for the symmetric rachet approach. finally, the protocol supports asynchronous communication and is capable of dynamically adapting to group changes such as user additions or removals, making it highly suitable for real-world applications where group dynamics are fluid.

articleTitle: AI Enabled Manufacturing: A Deep Learning Approach to Network Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Fault-tolerant control of industrial robotics network and highly connected machines setup for manufacturing in a production line is crucial. In this paper, we will discuss the recent advancements in fault-tolerant control strategies for collaborative robots with focus on the communication network faults. Cyber-attacks on robotic cyber physical systems (CPS) in the context of fourth industrial revolution constitutes a threat to the modern production systems which requires real-time detection so that the damage to the physical layer could be avoided. By selecting appropriate features for the deep neural network (DNN), it has been found that, an accuracy of 94.64% can be achieved for classifying malicious attacks. Thus, artificial intelligence (AI) can play a substantial role in securing future industrial manufacturing systems from cyber-threats thus avoiding down time in the production lines and large scale manufacturing operations.

articleTitle: Zero Trust Implementation for Legacy Systems using Dynamic Microsegmentation, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper, titled “Zero Trust Implementation for Legacy Systems using Dynamic Microsegmentation, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC),” addresses the critical cybersecurity challenges legacy systems pose. Legacy infrastructures, integral to numerous organizations, exhibit vulnerabilities due to obsolete security architectures. The paper proposes a novel approach by implementing a Zero Trust framework, incorporating dynamic microsegmentation, Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC). The objective is to establish a resilient security posture that adapts to real-time network changes, user behaviour, and evolving threat landscapes. The paper encompasses a comprehensive literature review, prototype design, and critical evaluation. The technical artefact, a prototype, showcases the application of cutting-edge cybersecurity concepts tailored for legacy systems. Ethical considerations guide the responsible development and evaluation of the prototype. The paper's forward-looking approach, including recommendations for enhancements, positions it as a valuable contribution to advancing cybersecurity practices in legacy environments.

articleTitle: A Combined Support Vector Machine and Statistical Method for Iris Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative hybrid method for iris recognition by combining a Modified Fuzzy C-Means (MFCM) algorithm with Support Vector Machine (SVM) techniques, aiming to improve both accuracy and efficiency. The research focuses on advancing iris recognition systems to strengthen security, enhance precision, and safeguard privacy in authentication and identification processes. The proposed method incorporates preprocessing techniques alongside classification strategies to enable precise identification of human iris patterns. Specifically, it utilizes MFCM and high-order statistical features for effective iris localization and feature extraction, followed by classification through Principal Component Analysis (PCA) integrated with SVM. Experimental results show that this approach significantly boosts the performance of iris recognition systems. Overall, the findings suggest that the proposed framework offers a reliable and secure solution, suitable for a wide range of identification and authentication applications.

articleTitle: A Blockchain Approach for Enhanced Traceability and Quality Assurance in Construction Supply Chains
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive framework leveraging blockchain technology to enhance traceability and quality assurance in construction supply chains. By utilizing decentralization, transparency, and immutability, the proposed approach ensures adherence to regulations and maintains data integrity throughout the supply chain. The methodology involves integrating a permissioned blockchain network for all stakeholders, standardizing data input, and utilizing smart contracts to automate compliance verification. The main findings demonstrate that blockchain technology significantly improves monitoring effectiveness, reduces operational inefficiencies, and promotes sustainable construction practices. Key results include enhanced data security, real-time access for stakeholders, and streamlined compliance checks. Challenges related to scalability and economic feasibility are also discussed, emphasizing the need for further research. This investigation highlights blockchain's potential to revolutionize supply chain management in the construction industry by improving accountability, efficiency, and transparency.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection in Smart Cities: Leveraging Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Enhanced Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The use of the internet is continuously expanding, and data has become a crucial asset in today's digital landscape. Smart Cities leverage technology to develop innovative solutions for addressing urban challenges, utilizing communication and information frameworks. However, Smart City applications are susceptible to various cyberattacks, such as Probing (Prob), Denial of Service (DOS), User to Root (U2R) and Remote to Local (R2L) attacks. Prominent examples for Smart Cities include New York City, Dubai, London, Barcelona, Singapore, and Tokyo. This study introduces a deep learning-based way for attacks detection in Smart Cities by Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. The NSL-KDD dataset is utilized to assess the suggested solution, while the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is activated to stem class imbalance. Experimental findings show that the model delivers high-performance metrics, achieving an accuracy of over 98.48%, a precision of 99%, a recall of 99%, and an F1-score of 98% on normalized data utilizing the SMOTE technique. These results focal point the validity of the proposed model in identifying attack traffic in Smart City environments.

articleTitle: Saudi Stock Market Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The research seeks to apply a particular approach to predicting a company's adjusted closing price in hopes of making an advancement in forecasting of the stock price. This research is significant due to its advantages to individuals, corporations, and governments. Approximating a stock's volatility is challenging for traders, and accurate predictions can help investors reduce portfolio risks. Stock prices do not behave in the linear manner. Thus, we suggest the application of artificial intelligence techniques, namely multilayer perceptron (MLP) and long short-term memory (LSTM), to model the changes in Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) index. This research aims at predicting the future of energy, telecommunication, financial, and industrial sectors of the stock exchange. The data was collected from Tadawul for the years 2018–2020 concerning these sectors. The AI algorithms aimed to predict the forthcoming benchmarks for the stock market sectors. The proposed models were tested against actual input data and simulation results, which produced extremely accurate results, demonstrating the effectiveness of the models. In addition, the correlation coefficient (R) of the MLP and LSTM models in predicting the values of Tadawul's four sectors integrated around 0.9950, signifying an exceptional correlation between forecasted and actual results. The forecasts were evaluated using four diverse trials, and between all the algorithms employed, LSTM produced the model's most precise predictions and best-fitting capacity.

articleTitle: IoT Network Security Framework to Classify RPL Attacks Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is an innovative concept that has become widely popular due to its numerous benefits. However, the Internet of Things (IoT) encounters numerous obstacles to ensuring security. RPL attacks pose a significant threat to the security of IoT networks, potentially compromising the integrity and functionality of interconnected devices and systems. Nevertheless, this growing dependence requires strong cybersecurity measures. We propose utilizing two deep learning models, namely GRU and LSTM-CNN. These models have been trained on the Contiki Cooja IoT simulator dataset. Furthermore, the SMOTE-ENN approach is utilized to balance the distribution of the attack classes in the dataset. The efficacy of the two proposed models is evaluated by taking into account their precision and F1-score. The findings show that the GRU and LSTM-CNN models exhibit 90% and 95% classification accuracies, respectively, in identifying RPL attacks.

articleTitle: YOLO-DRONE: Deep Learning Deployment for Drone Human Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), or drones, have become indispensable in surveillance, search and rescue, and border security operations due to their versatility and ability to navigate challenging environments. Despite advancements in drone technology, real-time human detection remains a significant challenge, constrained by computational limitations, environmental variability, and the demand for high-speed processing. This paper introduces an innovative human detection system powered by the lightweight YOLOv3-tiny deep learning algorithm, integrated into a UAV platform for efficient and accurate detection. The system balances real-time performance with computational efficiency, making it well-suited for resource-limited environments. Extensive experiments validate its reliability across diverse scenarios, including military zone monitoring and border patrol operations. The results demonstrate its potential to address key challenges in UAV applications, offering a scalable and effective solution for enhancing autonomous security and surveillance systems.

articleTitle: Vision Transformer with Attention Mechanism for Copy-Move Forgery Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to detecting and localizing copy-move forgery (CMF) in digital images using the BusterNet model enhanced with Vision Transformer (ViT) technology. Recognizing the limitations of traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in understanding the broader context of images, our study integrates the transformative capabilities of ViTs, renowned for their proficiency in capturing global dependencies through self-attention mechanisms. This hybrid model employs a dual-branch architecture focusing on both manipulation detection and similarity analysis to robustly address varied forgery scenarios. Extensive tests demonstrate that the BusterNet with ViT performs better than conventional methods, providing high precision, recall, and intersection over union (IoU) scores. These results underscore the model's efficacy in detecting sophisticated forgeries that conventional methods might miss, highlighting its potential for advancing digital image forensics.

articleTitle: Beyond Asymptotics: Real-Time Performance of Basic Operations (Preliminary Results)
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This paper presents preliminary findings on the real-time performance of fundamental mathematical operations, moving beyond traditional asymptotic analysis. While asymptotic analysis offers valuable insights into algorithms' theoretical behavior, it is equally important to consider real-world applications' practical performance and resource constraints. Our work empirically measures and analyzes the execution time of basic operations (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, etc.) across various data types and sizes, along with a basic Artificial Neural Network (ANN). The results emphasize the effect of size on the algorithm's overall performance, keeping in mind the complication of the operation itself. Our results focus on studying real-time performance beyond the theoretical analysis offered by asymptotic analysis are considered the building block for further research. Moreover, it lays the groundwork for a deeper understanding of real-time performance for scalable algorithms for real-time big data analytics where efficient execution of basic operations is essential. Also, applying adaptive optimization based on machine learning techniques for optimal performance. Using machine learning to predict the real-time cost of basic operations is an innovative approach.

articleTitle: CSRP Protocol for High Accuracy Performance in Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In recent years, Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) has played a broad role in many vital applications that are used to monitor environmental and physical events. One of the major issues in WSN is the overlapping region of sensing bands, which occurs due to densely and randomly deployed nodes in the target environment. The data aggregation technique is used as a solution that processes overlapping regions. This technique manages and redirects these data to the sink node through a multi-hop network. Therefore, the data transmission number and the duration toward the sink node are reduced, which fixes the overlapping region issue. However, using data aggregation techniques limited network performance due to energy consumption. The objective of this paper is to address this limitation by employing intelligent algorithms to enhance the operation strategies of data aggregation techniques. A protocol based on the Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering (HAC), Self-Organized Map (SOM), and Enhanced Radial Basis Function (ERBF) neural network is proposed in order to accomplish this goal. The clustered SOM and RBF-based Intelligent Protocol (CSRP) is the name of this proposed protocol. When compared to pertinent recent studies, the suggested protocol produced the best results in terms of the accuracy of the data arriving at the base station.

articleTitle: 3D Hand Gesture Detection Using Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: 3D hand gesture recognition has significantly improved human-computer interactions due to the advancement in deep learning, depth sensors, and artificial intelligence. These technologies have enhanced the development of convenient, compatible hand recognition interfaces, thereby making it possible for people with disabilities to interact with others efficiently. The aim of this paper is to evaluate and compare 3D hand gestures using several metrics such as execution time, training, testing, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value, and likelihood. Hence, this paper proposes the use of convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithms to recognize 3D hand gestures. Two people participated in the whole experiment, and a total of twelve 3D hand motions were recorded within a long distance. Experimental results show that the first participant in the single experiment and the second participant in the combined experiment have the best values in most parameters.

articleTitle: Improving Accuracy of Diabetes Prediction Using Machine Learning Techniques and Clinical Data
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic condition affecting millions of people globally, requiring early and accurate prediction to mitigate associated health risks. This study employed a Kaggle dataset with 96,148 records, preprocessed through normalization, encoding, and the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to address class imbalance. Two machine-learning models, Random Forest (RF) and Support Vector Machine (SVM), were trained and evaluated. Without addressing class imbalance, RF achieved 96.91% accuracy, with a lower computational time than SVM. After balancing the dataset, RF outperformed SVM with an accuracy of 95.42%, recall of 95.42%, and Area Under the Curve of 0.97, demonstrating superior performance in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. These results highlight RF as an optimal model for diabetes prediction, offering reliability and computational efficiency and making it a suitable choice for real-world healthcare applications.

articleTitle: NLP-Driven Detection of Cyber-Bullying Comments in Instagram Social Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: People's attention towards usage of social media is growing continuously, particularly youngsters are paying special attention by means of advancing their professions and expanding network. Cyber-bullying, includes posting derogatory comments on other people's posts, fabricating an identity, and disseminating embarrassing photos or videos, is also on the rise on social media. Victims of cyber-bullying may result in low self-esteem, increased suicidal thoughts, and other negative emotions like anxiety, frustration, fury, or sadness of the person. Undoubtedly numerous calculations like Machine Learning (ML) methods have been utilized in recognizing cyber-bullying exercises which remain totally frozen. The primary focus of the proposed work is to integrate Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) information retrieval method with a Random Forest (RF) classifier. TF-IDF decreases the dimensionality of the dataset by turning textual data into numerical features and concentrating on informative words. RF classifier handles the words with high TF-IDF scores in a corpus and classifies the comments as “Low” and “High” depending on the severity flagged as potential indicators of bullying behavior. This framework develops software which automatically identifies and prevents hateful comments and hides them from the victim's page. Compared to other classifiers, RF adapts many linguistic patterns, manages copious data generated on social platform and handles imbalances in cyberbullying comments, particularly when paired with class weighting or sampling approaches. This work mainly focusses on Instagram social media page where it accomplishes 88% of accuracy, 0.89 of precision, 0.94 of recall and 0.91 of F-measure in detection of harmful words.

articleTitle: A Novel Multifunctional Shunt Active Power Filter Based AI-Driven for Grid-Tied PV System using Z-Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Contemporary power systems face significant power quality (PQ) challenges due to the increasing prevalence of nonlinear loads, especially power electronics circuits. This research proposes a novel Shunt Active Power Filter (ShAPF) system that utilizes an advanced Z-source inverter (ZSI) topology combined with a grid-tied photovoltaic (PV). The proposed system offers a single-stage power conversion process, enhancing efficiency and reducing complexity and costs. By employing artificial intelligence (AI) control strategies, our system achieves superior performance in harmonic elimination, power factor (PF) correction, and current balancing simultaneously as a multifunctional operation, adhering to International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standards. This solution not only addresses power quality issues but also promotes sustainable energy integration, particularly benefiting rural microgrids in regions such as rural Africa.

articleTitle: Detecting Theft over Pattern Change Recognition and Locating Stolen Micro Mobility Vehicles in Uncovered Signals Areas
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Property theft, including vehicle theft, has become a significant concern globally. Technological advancements are providing smart solutions to address issues like vehicle theft. This research aims to enhance indoor localization by developing a solution for asset tracking. The emergence of micro-mobility vehicles, such as e-scooters and e-bikes, presents an opportunity to promote sustainable urban transportation. However, micro-mobility businesses—direct-to-consumer companies and sharing platforms—face significant challenges in fleet management and theft prevention. The present study proposes a “Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) beacon” solution to help these businesses protect their fleets, even in worst-case scenarios. The research objectives are twofold: to track stolen micro-mobility vehicles and to trace lost assets accurately, using a long transmission range of up to 500 meters. The proposed approach enables operators to accurately locate stolen scooters through indoor mapping, leveraging the BLE beacon's extended transmission range and a battery life of up to 20 years. Research designs consist of artifacts such as constructs, models, methods, and instantiations created to achieve the goals of scientific inquiry into the design. The artifact represents a comprehensive framework for improving asset tracing in challenging environments.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Low-Latency IoT Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Many sectors have been transformed by the growth of the Internet of Things devices, but it also presents difficulties, particularly in the latency of data exchange. In this research, I suggest a unique distributed federated learning architecture for low-latency Internet of Things communications. I empower IoT devices to jointly train machine learning models without compromising data privacy by utilizing federated learning techniques. To accomplish low-latency IoT communications, the architecture prioritizes communication efficiency optimization. Use Python to create this design and provide experimental data to show how successful.

articleTitle: A Secure Mutual Authentication Model in Fog Computing Based on Elliptic Curve
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Fog Computing presents a qualitative transformation in a decentralized computing architecture where different resources are located in various edge devices. This technique involves data processing in a centralized form and at the edge of the network to get trusted communication and approved authentication. This paper introduced a coherent mutual authentication with an adopted Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) to improve the security margin with a smaller ciphering key length. The proposed model ensures a secure and fast mutual authentication between the Fog nodes and end users. Moreover, the proposed model overcomes the shortcomings of traditional authentication approaches. The investigation and analysis of acquired results prove that the proposed model fulfills the security aspects and reduces the computational overhead. The results show that the proposed model mitigates security threats and risks like man-in-the-middle attacks and illegal access. The proposed model is suitable for IoT applications and restricted resources, where the lightweight asymmetric key cryptosystem has been applied. A revocation mechanism is also included in the proposed mechanism to prevent unauthorized access to fog nodes. A security and computational efficiency evaluation are performed along with a comparison with the existing authentication scheme.

articleTitle: The Synergy of Autoencoders and Electronic Health Records for Improved Patient Care
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Electronic health records have progressively replaced paper health records as a method of maintaining a competitive edge in the healthcare industry. Medical workers, including doctors and nurses, are responsible for establishing and maintaining electronic health records (EHRs) to guarantee the updating of patient information. These files include records such as diagnoses, prescriptions, treatment plans, imaging studies, test results, allergy information, and financial information. Electronic health records show potential for enhancing patient safety, treatment, engagement, and care coordination. Despite these advantages, the amount and complexity of the information included in electronic health records may be overwhelming. Researchers may employ unstructured data, such as clinical notes, in their study, although statistics and classifications are more often used. This large amount of data raises a variety of basic administrative and comprehension challenges. To address these difficulties, we must employ certain equipment and techniques. Machine learning has fundamentally altered the healthcare industry over the past ten years by delivering answers to challenges such as diagnosis, outcome prediction, treatment plan development, and population management. Machine learning enabled these breakthroughs. EHRs might benefit from new patterns, linkages, and insights provided by machine learning algorithms. The healthcare system may undergo significant changes if highly proficient computers trained on massive amounts of data can spot patterns, forecast outcomes, and make suggestions. Autoencoders may improve electronic health records' readability. The data display is more accurate, but it has less visibility. This might lead to an excellent EHR for patient grouping and other uses. We group data sets from electronic health records according to common characteristics. This category may contain patients' medical histories, treatment outcomes, and prognosis. With autoencoders, doctors may be able to better target specific patient groups, adapt therapy, and predict outcomes. We can do this by improving clustering efficiency. This work presents autoencoders for classifying data from electronic health records. The study's findings show that autoencoders might improve clinical judgment and allow for more personalized therapy. Because of deep learning and the huge amounts of data included in electronic health records, efficiency and quality of life in a constantly developing healthcare system are improved.

articleTitle: A Novel Remote Desktop Protocol Data Security Approach Using Hybrid Cryptographic Algorithm and Unsupervised Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: An empirical investigation uses AES, RSA, and a character replacement approach, along with the unsupervised neural network RBM, to enhance the security of Remote Desktop Protocol communication. It was discovered that Remote Access Trojans, such as PlugX, are used to establish control through remote access to compromised systems. Unauthorized access is obtained by an intruder to a system, resulting in the theft of sensitive data and the exploitation of a vulnerable workstation for malicious activities using a Remote Access Trojan (RAT). The proposed hybrid model is combined with RBM to ensure data transaction security between nodes. In addition, a comparative classification algorithm is integrated to further enhance the model. This study evaluates key size, data size, execution time, and memory usage of the algorithm. Cryptography is essentially a resource-intensive approach to computing security. Competitive and comparative analyses are being conducted to investigate the performance measures of the proposed model. In most cases, it was found that resource utilization was correlated with the key lengths of the AES and RSA algorithms. Due to the use of multiple categorical attacks on the remote desktop protocol, researchers have limited focus on secure data transaction of the remote desktop protocol. Therefore, the study limits the analysis of advanced security technologies that are used to gain a deeper understanding of the threats. This suggests that proposed algorithm is more reliable compared to AES and RSA when considering both security and efficacy. The research introduces a cutting-edge hybrid cryptographic model, enhanced with an unsupervised neural network, to outsmart potential intruders and protect sensitive data. By employing a Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM) for smart, autonomous threat recognition, the study assesses performance metrics crucial for real-world application and achieves a remarkable 98.75% accuracy, setting a new standard in RDP security.

articleTitle: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Access: Development and Assessment of an Open-Domain Medical Question Answering System with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Arabic open question answering system (OQAS) in health informatics (HI) can promote health education and support individuals in making informed decisions. It may contribute to health education and awareness initiatives by offering precise and reliable information. It enables individuals to comprehend health-related topics, preventative actions, and treatment alternatives in their preferred language. In addition, it facilitates the accessibility of pertinent health information to a broader audience, consequently addressing language barriers. There is a limited number of Arabic OQAS in HI. Thus, this study built an OQAS using graph convolutional network (GCN) and Transformers. The author conducted data preparation and extracted named entity-relationship (NER) from raw data. A graph generator was developed to represent the NER relationship for improving the efficiency of GCN in generating a required outcome. Similarly, Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT 2.0) was fine-tuned using the Hyperband optimization. Finally, the author integrated GCN and GPT 2.0 to improve the performance of the proposed model. The performance evaluation was conducted using the MAQA dataset. The experimental outcome highlighted the importance of the proposed OQAS in healthcare informatics. The extended fine-tuning of the proposed model could improve its interpretability.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Age and Gender Prediction Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have witnessed remarkable progress and are finding applications in diverse domains. This research paper introduces a novel application of BCI technology, focusing on the prediction of age and gender via EEG analysis using Deep CNN and ResNet models. A widely adopted EEG recording device was employed to capture cerebral activities from 64 subjects, encompassing both male and female participants, in a comfortable situation with eyes closed and eyes opened. The CNN model achieved an accuracy of 99.8% for age classification and 99.93% for gender classification. On the other hand, the ResNet model attained an accuracy of 99.05% for age and 99.32% for gender classification. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that utilizing all channels of the EEG signals yields superior performance in predicting age and gendercompared to brain regions.

articleTitle: Development of a Hand-Held Device for Women Assault Reporting
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The issue of insecurity is a major concern for women and society. The World Health Organisation's statistics show that about one in three women worldwide experience physical or sexual violence in their intimate or non-partner relationships. This is a disturbing figure. Various crimes against women such as physical violence, kidnapping, rape, sexual assault, and sexual harassment occur at different places at any given time of the day, especially in isolated places and mostly during late hours. These crimes contribute to the local and global crime indexes, as evidenced by the increasing criminality score. Governments have tried to address these security challenges by implementing stricter laws, but crime rates remain high. Unfortunately, related works exist but are limited as they lack critical features such as a secured and exclusive fingerprint verification for users, a subsystem to prevent a potentially detrimental false alarm from occurring, and an effective alerting mechanism to alert relatives. To overcome these shortcomings, this research proposes a hand-held device for women assault reporting that incorporates: a secured fingerprint verification subsystem, a vibration-based alert subsystem for prompting the user to prevent false alarms, an emergency text along with a phone call established to the predefined contacts as a more urgent alert mechanism, and a built-in microphone feature for environmental audio surveillance established via phone call connection. The system's response time was an average of 4 seconds, the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) was 6%, and the False Rejection Rate (FRR) was 5%. These promising results indicate that the system can effectively reduce crime against women, improve the sense of safety in women anywhere they go, and mitigate the overall crime rate.

articleTitle: Harmonic Minimization in Cascaded Multi-Level Inverter Using Invasive Weed Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study investigates the application of Invasive Weed Optimization (IWO), Harmony Search Algorithm (HSA), and Genetic Algorithm (GA) for optimizing switching angles in an eleven-level Cascaded Multi-Level Inverter (CMLI). The objective is to minimize low-order harmonic distortion in the output voltage for both single-phase and three-phase configurations. The research employs a comparative analysis to evaluate the effectiveness of these optimization algorithms in achieving optimal switching angles using Selected Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation (SHE-PWM). This approach minimizes Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) within the output voltage while adhering to predefined harmonic limits. The results of this comparative analysis will shed light on the strengths and weaknesses of each optimization technique for harmonic mitigation in CMLIs.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of State-of-the-Art Deep Neural Network on High-Resolution Medical Images
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: The growing accessibility and storage of high-resolution chest X-ray images in contemporary hospitals have generated unparalleled prospects for data-driven decision-making in healthcare. Nonetheless, the efficient application of deep learning models for precise diagnosis is hindered by the complex features and fine details inherent in these images. This study aims to tackle these problems by deploying and evaluating three sophisticated deep neural networks-Inception-ResNetV2, ResNet152, and DenseNet201-utilizing a meticulously selected dataset of chest X-ray pictures. The efficacy of neural networks is evaluated by many metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, Fl-score, and AUC-ROC, which illustrate their proficiency in picture classification tasks with high precision and accuracy. This study's findings yield significant insights into the strengths and shortcomings of each network, presenting possible opportunities for improving high-resolution image classification. Ultimately, these enhancements may provide more efficient and prompt diagnosis in healthcare environments.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Railway Ticketing: Enhancing Security and Efficiency with QR Codes and Smart Contract
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: In light of the increasing prevalence of railway ticketing fraud, it is imperative to implement advanced technological solutions to guarantee the integrity and security of ticket transactions. The blockchain technology's decentralized, transparent, and immutable record-keeping method has the potential to address these problems. The utilization of blockchain technology in railway ticketing systems is being analyzed with the aim of enhancing the detection and prevention of fraudulent activities. Smart contracts ensure the security of each transaction by enabling quick verification and minimizing issues such as ticket duplication, illegal modifications, and counterfeit tickets. A blockchain system guarantees the genuineness and validity of tickets for passengers, railway personnel, and ticketing agencies. The report also explores the incorporation of blockchain technology into rail ticketing systems as an adaptable and robust remedy for fraud. Resolving challenges related to the deployment of scalability, data protection, and regulatory compliance. The study conducts a simulation and analysis of the blockchain-based system, revealing a substantial reduction in fraudulent activities. The findings of our study demonstrate that the system effectively eradicates ticket fraud, enhances operational efficiency, and is financially feasible with an adoption cost of $3.54. This enhances the efficiency and reliability of train ticketing.

articleTitle: Optimizing Research Performance: The Impact of ChatGPT and Digital Competence on Research Skills and Autonomy
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: Leveraging Self-Determination Theory to comprehend their implications on perceived skills and autonomy, this study attempts to investigate the impact of digital competence and AI tools such as ChatGPT on research performance. Research performance, perceived autonomy, digital competency, ChatGPT use, and perceived research skills are all included into the suggested model. 426 replies were received from a survey held at universities in Saudi Arabia, and 386 valid instances were examined using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that ChatGPT use and perceived research skills are highly correlated with digital competence, and that these factors improve research performance and perceived autonomy. According to the study, using ChatGPT enhances researchers' perceptions of research skills and autonomy and research skills, both of which are essential for effective research performance. With 46.5% of the variance in research performance explained by the model, it has a moderate level of explanatory power. In order to meet basic psychological demands like perceived competence and perceived autonomy–both of which are critical for academic success–this research emphasizes the significance of digital competence and AI tools. In order to empower researchers and maximize results, the study emphasizes the crucial role that digital literacy and AI tools play in improving research performance by meeting basic psychological requirements. It also stresses the significance of integrating new technologies in academia. It provides theoretical and practical understanding of the relationship between research effectiveness and digital competency.

Author Keywords: ChatGPT as a Research Support Tool

articleTitle: Enhancing Organizational Performance through Big Data Analytics: The Critical Roles of Knowledge Processes and Management Capability
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of big data analytics (BDA) on organizational performance (OP), emphasizing the mediating roles of knowledge acquisition (KAC), knowledge conversion (KCO), and knowledge application (KAP), along with the moderating role of big data analytics management capability (BDAMC). Anchored in a positivist paradigm and guided by a deductive approach, the research utilizes a cross-sectional survey design within a quantitative framework. Data were collected from 384 professionals employed in the Bangladeshi telecommunications industry. The survey findings were analyzed using SPSS 26 and Smart-PLS 4.0 to evaluate the proposed model. The analysis indicates a strong and positive relationship between BDA and OP. Additionally, KAC, KCO, and KAP were found to partially mediate this relationship, while BDAMC enhanced the strength of the connection between BDA and OP. The study makes a significant theoretical contribution by extending the application of Dynamic Capabilities Theory and offering valuable insights for telecommunications leaders aiming to leverage BDA for improved operational efficiency, competitive advantage, and sustainable growth.

articleTitle: Use of Machine Learning to Forecast Solar and Wind Energy Production for NEOM City
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: NEOM, one of prominent future project of the Saudi Arabia, set to be the World's largest carbon-free system and globally leading hub to the clean energy, aiming to be powered entirely by renewable energy sources primarily solar and wind. Considering its geographic position which offers abundant solar irradiance and strong coastal winds, accurate forecasting of energy production is critical to ensure consistent energy supply, also for the effective integration of renewable resources into NEOM's smart energy infrastructure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is not only supporting renewable energy generation but also improving its reliability, efficiency, and scalability in order to make solar and wind energy a viable mainstream source. This study presents a comprehensive AI based approach to forecast solar and wind energy production in NEOM, utilizing advanced machine learning models and statistical methods, such as time series analysis, artificial neural networks (ANN), and hybrid forecasting models. By integrating historical weather data, satellite observations, and real-time environmental monitoring, precise predictions has been developed for solar irradiance and wind speed, both are critical for optimizing the performance of photovoltaic systems and wind turbines. The results demonstrate that provided methods are capable to enhance forecasting precision, and support to handle the dynamic energy needs of a city designed for renewable self-sufficiency.

articleTitle: Efficient Adjustable Routing Path for Data Collection in Underwater Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2025 4th International Conference on Computing and Information Technology (ICCIT)
abstract: UWSNs, already, have diverse marine applications which include environmental monitoring, Coastal oil exploration, and disaster prevention, among others.
